# Soil Health and Sustainable Agriculture

## Overview

This project page highlights USDA Sustainable Agriculture Research and Education experience involving soil health, beneficial microorganisms, Rhizobium, compost and soil samples, crop productivity, field preparation, irrigation, wet lab work, and farmer outreach.

## Research Context

Soil health research connects biological, chemical, and physical soil processes with agricultural productivity and sustainable land management. Beneficial microorganisms can influence nutrient cycling, soil function, and crop performance, making this experience relevant to restoration, agriculture, organic certification, soil science, and environmental monitoring roles.

## Activities

- Collected soil and compost samples for microbial DNA extraction and laboratory analysis.
- Assisted with field preparation, drip irrigation installation, seed propagation, and plot maintenance.
- Supported research involving beneficial microorganisms, Rhizobium, soil amendments, crop productivity, and sustainable agriculture.
- Maintained research plots through irrigation, weed management, pest monitoring, and field maintenance.
- Presented research concepts to Florida farmers and agricultural stakeholders.
